vendor: sst / anomalyco — OpenCode (opencode.ai), upstream `anomalyco/opencode` (dev branch, CLI v2.1.1, CHANGELOG v2.1.0 dated 2026-10-20)
surfaces: Terminal TUI/CLI (`opencode` / `opencode2`, Windows binaries `opencode.exe`, `opencode2.exe`, `opencode2-node.exe`), OpenCode Desktop (Electron), ACP agent integration (packages/cli/src/acp), VS Code SDK (sdks/vscode). All surfaces share one machine-wide SQLite DB.
binaries: `opencode` (npm `@opencode/cli`, ships `bin/opencode.cjs`; native release is `opencode.exe` on Windows — packages/cli/script/publish.ts:68), `opencode2` (Node build, `opencode2-node.exe`)

storage.format: SQLite (Drizzle ORM over Bun/Node sqlite). Tables: `session_v2`, `session_message`, `event`, `event_sequence`, `project`, `project_directory`, `worktree`, `workspace`, `kv`, `permission`, `credential`. Message/event payloads are plaintext JSON in TEXT columns. NOT JSONL, NOT JSON-per-file. The historical JSON storage (`~/.local/share/opencode/storage/{session,message,part}/*.json`) no longer exists upstream — it was replaced by SQLite, then migrated again by `database/v1-migration.bun.ts` from v1 tables `session`/`message`/`part` into `session_v2`/`session_message`/`event`.
storage.append_semantics: Not line-append. Two granularities exist: (1) the `event` table is an append-only durable event log — one INSERT per durable event, `seq` monotonic per sessionID, `created` = epoch ms, never updated; (2) `session_message` rows are INSERTed when a step starts and then UPDATEd in place as text/tool state streams (projector.ts:247 insert, projector.ts:262 update). DB runs `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` (database.ts:40), so live writes land in `opencode.db-wal` and the main file is rewritten at checkpoints — a byte-offset file tailer is useless here.
storage.session_file_naming: One DB per machine, not per project: `%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db` (XDG-style on Windows too: packages/util/src/global-roots.ts uses `XDG_DATA_HOME || ~/.local/share`, no %LOCALAPPDATA%/%APPDATA% branch anywhere in packages/). Filename = `opencode.db` (channels latest/dev/beta/next/prod) or `opencode-<channel>.db`; overridable by `OPENCODE_DB` (packages/cli/src/database-path.ts). Sessions are ROWS (`session_v2.id` = `ses_…`), not files; there is no per-project subdirectory.

fields.project: YES — `session_v2.directory` (absolute cwd, forward-slashed) and `session.created` event `data.location.directory`; project name = last path component (repo: packages/core/src/session/sql.ts:35, packages/schema/src/location.ts:9)
fields.model: YES — `session_v2.model` = {id, providerID, variant?} and assistant message `model` (Model.Ref) plus `session.model.selected` event
fields.file_basename: YES — tool input keys: `path` for read/write/edit/glob/grep (current upstream name; older builds used `filePath`), `patchText` for `patch` (packages/core/src/tool/plugin/edit.ts:22, write.ts:25, read.ts:20)
fields.tool_activity: YES — `session.tool.called` event carries tool `name` + full `input` object; `session.tool.success`/`failed` are terminal; `shell` message carries `command`
fields.phase: YES — `session.execution.started` (turn begins, also sets the claim) / `.succeeded` / `.failed` / `.interrupted`; projected `session_message` type=`idle` with outcome

parser_strategy:
Do NOT reuse the JSONL tailer. Two options; recommended = (1).

(1) EVENT-TABLE POLLER (recommended). Read `%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db` read-only with rusqlite and poll the append-only `event` table, which is already an ordered, timestamped, per-session log.
  - Active session: `SELECT id, directory, model, agent FROM session_v2 WHERE time_suspended IS NOT NULL ORDER BY time_suspended DESC LIMIT 1` (time_suspended is the execution claim: set on session.execution.started, cleared on terminal — packages/core/src/session/store.ts:208-227). Fallback when no claim: newest `session_v2` by `time_updated` within N minutes.
  - New events: `SELECT seq, type, data, created FROM event WHERE aggregate_id = ?1 AND seq > ?2 ORDER BY seq ASC` (seq = watermark; `created` = epoch ms; data = JSON payload).
  - Emit each row as a SYNTHETIC JSON LINE and feed it through the existing contract: `serde_json::to_string(&row)` → `parse_line_for(Provider::OpenCode, line)`. This keeps `parse_line_for` as the single parsing entry point and makes unit tests use real upstream row shapes. The synthetic line is `{"id":…,"aggregate_id":…,"seq":…,"created":…,"type":…,"data":{…}}` — i.e. the upstream row itself.
  - Mapping (raw event type → ParsedEvent):
    * `session.created` → SessionMetadata{project: basename(data.location.directory), cwd: data.location.directory}
    * `session.execution.started` → TaskStarted{started_at_ms: created}
    * `session.step.started` → Thinking{reasoning: None} (phase = thinking) + AgentDetected{agent: "providerID/modelID"} from data.model
    * `session.model.selected` → AgentDetected{agent: "providerID/modelID" (charset-sanitized, ≤128 chars, no prose)}
    * `session.agent.selected` → AgentDetected{agent: data.agent}
    * `session.tool.called` → TrackedToolStarted{call_id: data.id, activity: {label: classify_tool(name.to_lowercase(), input.command), file: basename(input.path|input.filePath), language: language_from_file(file)}} — file basename ONLY
    * `session.tool.success` | `session.tool.failed` → TrackedToolFinished{call_id: data.id}
    * `session.shell.started` → ToolStarted{activity: classify_tool("shell", data.command)}; `session.shell.ended` → ToolFinished
    * `session.execution.succeeded` | `.failed` | `.interrupted` → Completed
    * `session.tool.input.started` / `.input.ended` (raw arg text), `session.text.*`, `session.reasoning.*`, `session.tool.success` content → NO events (never map to anything; the raw text never leaves the parser)
  - Tool name → label uses the EXISTING `classify_tool` helper (edit/write/patch→"Editing files", read→"Reading project files", grep/glob→"Searching project", shell→command-derived safe labels). `extract_file_basename` already understands the key `path` (events.rs:659) so OpenCode's `path` arg works with no helper change; add `filePath` only if a legacy DB is encountered.
  - PRIVACY: only basename + fixed label + model id + phase + start time leave the parser. Never forward data.input.oldString/newString/content/patchText/command, never content[].text, never event `session.tool.input.ended.text`.

(2) `session_message` PROJECTION READ (fallback if the `event` table is missing): poll `session_message` for the active session (`ORDER BY seq`), take the last assistant row, and map its `data.content[]` entries of type "tool" (state.status running→TrackedToolStarted with state.input.path; completed/error→TrackedToolFinished with the tool id), `data.time.completed`/finish→Completed, `data.model`→AgentDetected, `data.type` "idle"→Completed. This path is strictly worse (rows are UPDATEd in place, so ordering/dedup is fiddlier) but needs the same SQLite dependency, so option (1) is preferred.

Discodex side (read-only, unmodified): src/provider.rs:348-395 (session_sources/is_session_log), src/events.rs:49-57 (parse_line_for dispatch), src/watcher.rs:22-140 (LogTailer byte-offset + zstd, recent_logs depth-5 scan), src/state.rs:113-259 (ActivityState::apply, Phase{Thinking,RunningTools}), src/main.rs:246-280 (startup scan) and 457-473 (notify → tailer.read_new).
risks: NEW DEPENDENCY: reading the DB needs a SQLite crate. rusqlite with the `bundled` feature compiles SQLite from C source (MSVC build tools required, slower clean builds); the lighter `rusqlite` without bundled needs a system SQLite DLL that Windows does not ship; `sqlx` is heavier. This is the single biggest cost of the adapter and should be an explicit decision, not a footnote.

NOT TAILABLE: the existing LogTailer is byte-offset/line based. The DB is a single binary file whose live writes go to opencode.db-wal in WAL mode and whose main file is rewritten at checkpoints. Feeding it to the tailer yields binary garbage and a permanent cursor desync. The adapter needs a poller, and notify on Windows is unreliable for SQLite page writes — poll on a timer instead.

SCHEMA CHURN: OpenCode V2 renames/reshapes tables often (session→session_v2, message/part→session_message/event, 50+ migrations in 2026 alone, weekly cadence). A hardcoded table/column set will silently break. Mitigation: probe sqlite_master + PRAGMA table_info at open time and disable the adapter (falling back to the existing focused-window detection) when the expected shape is absent.

PATH CHURN: the DB filename depends on the release channel (opencode.db vs opencode-<channel>.db) and can be relocated wholesale by OPENCODE_DB; the data dir moves with XDG_DATA_HOME. Mitigation: probe the data dir for opencode*.db and also honour XDG_DATA_HOME; skip -wal/-shm sidecars.

WAL READ SEMANTICS: a read-only connection to a WAL database needs write access to the -shm index (satisfied when the same user runs both) and can hit SQLITE_BUSY while opencode checkpoints; handle by skipping the tick and keeping the last state, never by crashing or blocking the publisher.

PRIVACY: `session.tool.called.data.input` contains full absolute paths and oldString/newString/content; `session.tool.input.ended.data.text` contains the raw arg JSON; `session.tool.success.data.content` contains tool output; assistant `content[].text` contains model output; `session_v2.title` contains the user's prompt subject. All of these are inside the same JSON blob the parser must read, so the parser must whitelist fields aggressively and never serialize whole rows.

LEGACY INSTALLS: pre-V2 OpenCode used the JSON storage dir (~/.local/share/opencode/storage/{session,message,part}/*.json) and an intermediate SQLite schema (session/message/part tables). Those are not the current format; supporting them means a second parser. Recommendation: target the current schema only, and gate on schema probe rather than on a legacy path.

MULTI-PROCESS / MULTI-SESSION: one machine-wide DB holds sessions for many projects at once, so 'the active session' must be selected deliberately (execution claim, then recency). Picking the wrong session would show a stale project in Discord.

ICON: the lobehub `opencode` asset has no brand folder in @lobehub/icons@1.97.0 and is a low-fidelity recolour of the mark; if the Discodex convention demands a per-product verified asset, use the official https://opencode.ai/favicon-96x96-v3.png instead.
confidence: medium-high. The storage model, schema, event semantics, tool arg names, and Windows path layout were read directly from upstream source at dev @ CLI v2.1.1 (not inferred), and the icon/asset URLs were HTTP-verified. Residual uncertainty: the exact on-disk filename on a user machine (channel variant, OPENCODE_DB, XDG_DATA_HOME), whether the user's opencode build is V2 (SQLite) or legacy V1 (JSON storage), and the practical read behaviour of a WAL DB from a second process on Windows (busy/‑shm). No local harness data directory was inspected, per instruction.
summary: OpenCode keeps ALL session state locally, but not in a line-delimited log: since OpenCode V2 everything lives in a single machine-wide SQLite database at %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db (XDG layout, same on Windows; overridable via OPENCODE_DB; channel builds use opencode-<channel>.db). The DB holds a durable, append-only `event` table (seq per session, epoch-ms `created`, JSON payload) plus live-updated `session_message` and `session_v2` projections. It therefore contains everything Discodex needs — workspace dir (session_v2.directory), model (session_v2.model / Model.Ref), current file (tool input `path`), tool name + args (session.tool.called), turn boundaries (session.execution.started/succeeded/failed), and a task-start timestamp — so richness is "rich" (project + file + tool activity + phase + timer + model). The cost is machinery: the existing byte-offset/JSONL tailer is unusable on a binary, WAL-mode, checkpoint-rewritten SQLite file, so the adapter needs a new DB poller plus a new `rusqlite` (bundled) dependency, and the poller must read the `event` table by seq watermark rather than tail bytes. Privacy holds: only basename + fixed label + model id + phase + start time are derivable; prompts, tool output, raw args and full paths stay in the DB.
